host: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 x64; WSL Ubuntu 24.04 for both disposable homeservers
notes: Passing tests do not establish a secure product.
Historical failures are retained; the hardened Merovingian build and live checks subsequently passed.

Windows environment admission is fixed and current restriction checks ran. An endpoint-observed network differential, run under three worker policies, shows the zero-capability AppContainer worker is not network-denied (closed ports refuse it; listener-side filtering only). A comparative LPAC run breaks Winsock initialization but still opens the AFD socket device. A third policy, an AppContainer whose base is a write-restricted, untrusted-integrity restricted token launched with CreateProcessAsUserW, cannot initialize (STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED) and yields no running worker. No tested policy denies the kernel socket; the full gate fails.

Normal-process encrypted-store restart and initial capability-selected native/classic sync now pass; real classic-only Synapse and controlled origins for both servers were tested. Runtime renegotiation, crash/corruption recovery, cross-signing, SDK-wide drain, transport containment and packaged cross-platform controls remain open.
No production homeserver contacted; disposable runners stopped after checks.
Current checks and hashes describe the component-based layout; historical_checks and pre_reorganization hashes retain earlier run provenance. Reorganization does not complete P0.

Retained task ownership and controlled real-SDK lifecycle barriers pass 12 new tests. SDK initialization waits and pause are not global drain barriers; the SDK completion contract remains unresolved. See sdk-lifecycle.json. No live homeserver scenarios were rerun for this step.
hash_normalization: Text manifest and lock hashes normalize CRLF to LF, matching repository attributes.
